changedBeliefs: The INTRINSIC send-vs-Isolate.exit transfer cost is now measured cleanly (prepared-result barrier: worker builds+holds the real ResultSet, main times Go-sent -> received as first op, one process per observation, ABBA, empty-envelope control). Three facts: (1) Isolate.exit has a ~47 us FIXED-overhead premium over send (empty envelope 147 vs 100 us) from its sendability walk + isolate teardown/reassignment; (2) strings/immutable leaves are SHARED on send, not copied — a 400 KB string adds ~0 us to send (payload -4), a 1 MB string +18 us; (3) send's copy cost is driven by the MUTABLE flat-list SLOT COUNT (pointer-array backing), not payload bytes — send payload rises 27 -> 163 -> 636 us across 20k -> 48k -> 200k int slots but is ~zero for a single huge string.

The send/exit CROSSOVER is ~48k structural slots (4-col numeric): send wins below (num20k send 127 vs exit 189), exit wins above (num48k 263 vs 241; num10kx20 200k-slots 736 vs 391 = -345 us). Because strings are shared free on send, string-heavy and low-slot-count results always favor send (lower fixed overhead); large mutable-structure results favor exit (zero-copy beats the growing slot-count copy). This is the intrinsic mechanism exp 241 could not isolate through its confounded pool harness, and it matches exp 241's noisy ~32k-slot crossover, now pinned at ~48k.

Send-vs-sacrifice is RESOLVED by combining this with exp 244 (pool capacity: no penalty at pool-4, sacrifice neutral-to-favorable). Small-to-moderate results (<~48k slots) and ALL string-heavy results are send-equivalent within the pre-registered equivalence margin (39-71 us diffs < +/-75-100 us) — the middle is a declared wash with a slight send lean. Large structural results (>~48k slots) materially favor exit (-203 to -345 us). The current sacrifice policy's INTENT (sacrifice large, send small) is validated; the DEFECT is only the trigger.
nextSignals: ACTIONABLE, and the one shippable win the whole send-vs-sacrifice arc produced: the sacrifice trigger keys on estimated BYTES, but the true intrinsic cost driver is MUTABLE STRUCTURAL SLOT COUNT (strings are shared free on send). So a large STRING (e.g. 400 KB, one slot) is send-favored (96 vs 167 us intrinsic) yet is wrongly sacrificed at the 256 KB byte threshold, AND pays a reader respawn for nothing. Follow-up experiment: route the sacrifice decision on mutable slot count instead of estimated bytes, or minimally add a shared-leaf guard that keeps string-heavy results on send. Fixes the misroute without touching the large-structural regime where exit correctly wins.

The send-vs-sacrifice DIRECTION is otherwise closed: intrinsic transfer (this run) + pool capacity (exp 244) both resolved, and both point the same way. Do NOT re-open with more through-the-pool A/Bs (exp 241's confound) or with attempts to retire sacrifice wholesale (exp 244 showed it is favorable at pool-4 for large results, this run shows it is the correct intrinsic choice above ~48k slots). Consider updating the result-transfer-shape synthesis in signals/base.json on the next curation pass to record the resolved mechanism.

Reusable measurement pattern established for any future intrinsic isolate-transfer question: prepared-result barrier (build + hold BEFORE a Go barrier), one fresh PROCESS per observation (kills heap accumulation / mode carryover), ABBA blocks, empty-envelope control to separate fixed overhead from payload cost, timestamps kept on one isolate (main) for clock comparability. This is the clean alternative to through-the-pool alternation, which is a state-changing treatment that cannot isolate transfer.
